local_checks.invariant: Pre-auth sign-in attempts are bounded so they cannot spend shared persistent resources without limit.
local_checks.result: Candidate sign-in with an unlisted email does 1 read (candidateSigninPaused) plus 1 D1 upsert (candidateUnknownEmail -> recordFailure -> countStmt) per request, up to CANDIDATE_UNKNOWN_PER_IP=200 per network per 10-minute window; then that network is paused and further attempts cost 1 read (src/lib/ratelimit.ts:47, 97-121, 284-295; src/routes/candidate.ts:43-49; src/routes/candidate-docs.ts:200-205). Admin sign-in does up to 3 upserts per attempt, bounded per network (20 per 15 min) and per account (5 per network, 50 per hour globally). PBKDF2 runs only for an existing named account, after counting. Every bound is per network (an IPv4 address or an IPv6 /64). No bound covers all networks together.

local_checks.invariant: The in-Worker request ceilings protect the shared, account-wide daily allowances that both sites depend on during a live test.
local_checks.result: RL_IP allows 3000 requests per minute per network (wrangler.toml:40-42, 150-152) and runs inside the Worker (src/index.ts:26-28), so a refused request is still a Worker invocation. local_checks.result: gradeCandidate (src/routes/admin.ts L1420-1555) and the writers grader (src/routes/admin-docs.ts L379-397) make one chatJson call per answer. Each call contains only that candidate's answer plus admin-authored question, rubric and reference fields. The result is written with candidate_id and question_id bound from the DB row, not taken from model output. Interview generation (admin.ts L171-187) uses only that candidate's resume fields and answers, and writes to that candidate_id. No batch prompt mixes candidates.

local_checks.invariant: Deterministic bounds on model-driven grading output: an answer cannot close the quoted block, and the score cannot exceed the question maximum.
local_checks.result: The boundary is a fresh ANSWER-<randomUUID> per request. Any occurrence of it is stripped from the answer (L259, L274; L368, L379). The score is reconciled with the deductions, snapped to 0.25 and clamped to [0, maxMarks] (L290-302, L388-394). ai_content_percent is clamped to 0-100. Persuasive answer text can still sway the model's judgement within those bounds, but only for the candidate's own answer, and a guardrail prompt is the only control there. That is inherent to LLM grading, not a code-level boundary failure.

local_checks.invariant: The candidate allowlist email taken from a resume is checked deterministically and cannot be invented by the model, and it cannot collide with an existing candidate.
local_checks.result: src/routes/admin.ts L599-611 accepts the model's email only if it literally appears in the extracted text or link annotations (emailsInText, src/lib/resume.ts L40-44); otherwise it falls back to the first literal email. It rejects in-batch duplicates and emails already used by another candidate, and the UNIQUE constraint backs this up. A resume author can only pick an email that their own resume contains, which they could equally print visibly. This is the deliberate product trust in resume content, not a model boundary. nameFromResume (L211-217) applies the same literal-in-text rule to the name.
